newsitem.title: CHINA: China says labour abuses still rampant.
newsitem.headline: China says labour abuses still rampant.

text.p: China said on Monday that labour abuses such as forced overtime, delayed payment of salaries and poor safety conditions were still major problems despite a law banning such practices.
A recent inspection of the implementation of China's labour law uncovered many violations of the rights granted to workers by the regulations, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Among the problems were excessive overtime hours, delayed payment of salaries, and safety and sanitary conditions that did not meet mandated standards, Xinhua said.
A stagnant social insurance system, rising unemployment and abuses of women's rights in the workplace were also common problems, the agency said.

Zhang Dinghua, vice-chairman of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions, urged China's trade unions to help workers draw up collective contracts with their employers to help protect their legal rights, it said.
The federation called on Chinese enterprises to sign collective contracts with their workers, Zhang said.
About 76,000 enterprises had signed collective contracts by the end of September, and more than 40 percent of foreign-funded firms had been required to sign contracts, Xinhua said.
